topic: Listening to the body: sleep debt, accumulated fatigue and the same nagging spot keep speaking, but we talk over them with the plan on paper; we listen first, then decide how hard to train today, without turning it into an excuse to skip
figure: Zeno of Citium, founder of Stoicism c. 334-262 BC (Diogenes Laertius, Lives 7.23: to a youth talking nonsense, the reason we have two ears and only one mouth is that we may listen more and talk less). Paraphrased, not quoted. Single quote page, at Mintra's request

slides.kicker: ZENO OF CITIUM · FOUNDER OF STOICISM
